articles.title: In a streaming wars world, JustWatch has become an essential tool
articles.summary: With the ever-increasing number of different streaming services and shifting rights battles, JustWatch — a search engine that tells you where any show or movie is available to stream — has become an essential tool for navigating the streaming wars.
articles.body: There are too many streaming services, and all of them are fighting over content that feels like it’s bouncing back and forth between streaming sites on a daily basis. This has made sites like JustWatch — a streaming search engine and recommendation site — an essential tool as more and more of these services continue to launch. JustWatch isn’t a new service; it’s been around since 2014. But the modern-day glut of streaming services and spiraling rights agreements have made it more essential than ever. At its core, JustWatch is a search engine for digital media. Type in a movie or TV show, and it’ll tell you everywhere you can stream it, watch it for free with ads, buy, or rent it. Once you’ve found what you’re looking for, you simply click and it’ll link you directly to that service. It’s not the only site or app that does this, but I’ve found it to be far and away the most reliable and useful. And that’s for a few reasons. The first is simply how comprehensive JustWatch is. It loops in basically every streaming service and TV show / movie seller under the sun — even ones that I had forgotten existed. Did I remember that CW Seed is a real website? Absolutely not, but it turns out it’s the only place you can currently stream the criminally underrated Pushing Daisies, something that I only learned from checking JustWatch. The site is also super up to date. HBO Max, for example, was already showing up in JustWatch results on the first day it was available. And seemingly no service is too obscure for JustWatch: it even has Quibi shows! [Image: But what sets it above and beyond the rest is that you can also filter searches based on specific streaming services. Only subscribe to Hulu and Netflix? Your search results will only show those services, if you want. You can also use more advanced filters, sorting by just movies or TV shows, IMDB rating, or MPAA age ratings, too. Only interested in 4K? JustWatch can tell you if it’s available or not. And if the movie you want isn’t available to stream somewhere, JustWatch also shows prices from basically every major retailer for renting or buying a film digitally. That’s extremely useful for comparing prices, whether you’re interested in building out your own digital library or just want the cheapest place to rent Bill & Ted’s Excellent Adventure this weekend. JustWatch isn’t just limited to US services: it’s available in over 45 countries around the world, including Canada and the United Kingdom. That makes it crucial in the streaming wars because what content is available, where it’s streaming, and even which services are available can shift wildly depending on what country you’re in. (For example, Star Trek: Discovery is a CBS All Access exclusive in the US, but available on Netflix in the UK.) With streaming catalogs continuing to shift and change over the coming months and years (just ask WarnerMedia, which has already had to amend HBO Max advertisements to note some movies will soon be leaving the service or aren’t available yet), finding who has the rights to the movie you want to watch is only going to get more difficult. And while nothing short of shifting market forces is likely to change that anytime soon, at least there are services like JustWatch to help sort out the chaos.

articles.title: Tech stocks today: CEOs call for pacing AI, as Nvidia CEO says extinction fears are made up
articles.summary: Tech stock news for the week of Sept. 14.
articles.body: Tech stocks fell in early trading on Tuesday, as the AI industry continues to grapple with warnings that the technology could eventually harm humans. The Nasdaq (^IXIC) fell roughly 0.2%.The episode began last week when an Anthropic researcher announced he was leaving the company on X, saying he didn't feel the company was doing enough to keep AI in check.Anthropic Alignment Science Lead Evan Hubinger responded to the post, saying the former Anthropic worker is correct and that he believes there is a greater-than-10 % chance that the technology could "kill all humans."On Saturday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei posted an essay responding to the posts, calling on AI companies to slow the pace of frontier AI development. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman agreed.But on Monday's All In podcast, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said that the fears of an AI doomsday scenario are simply made up.The various announcements raised questions about whether the AI buildout will continue at its breakneck pace, or if slowing frontier AI models could cut into it.

articles.standfirst: Descubre a continuación cuál es el número de la ONCE de hoy en el sorteo del cupón diario y comprueba los resultados del resto de juegos
articles.summary: A continuación puedes comprobar el cupón diario de la ONCE así como los resultados del resto de sorteos de hoy
articles.body: El juego más antiguo de los sorteos de la Organización Nacional de Ciegos Españoles (ONCE) es el sorteo del cupón diario de la ONCE, que ofrece hasta 55 premios que pueden llegar a los 35.000 euros para aquellos que acierten el número de 5 cifras. Junto a este premio se juega 'La Paga', que como su nombre indica, quien se hace con ella recibe una Paga de 3.000 euros al mes durante 25 años si además de acertar el cupón diario acierta el número de serie que acompaña al boleto. El número que ha resultado agraciado con el premio del cupón diario de la ONCE es el: Número de la ONCE: 33548 El número de serie que premia 'La Paga': 032 Los sorteos de la ONCE comenzaron en cada provincia de manera independiente. Su coste solía oscilar entre las 10 y las 25 pesetas. El sorteo entonces consistía en un número de tres cifras y una serie de hasta 5 cifras. En la actualidad, el sorteo de la ONCE ha cambiado, con un número de cinco cifras y tres números para la serie. En 1985 cambiaron los sorteos de fin de semana: el viernes se celebra el Cuponazo de la ONCE, con premios de hasta 9 millones de euros, y el sábado y domingo se juega el Sueldazo de la ONCE, con un premio único de 300.000 euros y una paga de 5000 euros durante 20 años. El sorteo del Super ONCE se celebra cinco veces al día de lunes a domingo. Está organizado por la Organización Nacional de Ciegos Españoles (ONCE). Los sorteos se celebran después del Triplex, cinco veces al día. Primer sorteo: 06-07-11-14-19-34-37-48-52-55-57-60-61-65-70-72-73-79-82-83 Segundo sorteo: 02-03-10-12-23-30-31-46-48-49-51-58-62-63-64-72-80-82-84-85 Tercer sorteo: 01-04-05-09-15-17-22-23-27-36-38-51-53-56-61-73-78-79-80-84 Cuarto sorteo: 05-07-11-13-18-20-34-39-44-46-56-58-59-62-63-65-67-73-79-85 Quinto sorteo: 04-07-10-14-17-18-19-21-23-24-25-32-40-42-58-62-67-70-75-79 El coste mínimo de la apuesta del Super ONCE es de 1 euro, pero se puede ganar hasta un millón de euros por cada euro apostado. En la apuesta se seleccionan números en un intervalo de 5 a 11, y podemos escoger desde el 1 hasta el 50. Estos números pueden usarse en un solo sorteo o en varios consecutivos. En los sorteos se extraen un total de 20 números que son los que determinan las combinaciones ganadoras. Los premios del Super ONCE dependen de los aciertos que lleve el participante en su boleto y la cantidad de números que haya apostado. Se obtiene un premio mayor si la cantidad de números apostados y números acertados es similar, es decir, si se apuesta a 7 números y se aciertan los 7, el premio es más grande que si se apuesta por 8 y se aciertan siete. También depende del dinero que se apueste. El premio es mayor si se apuestan 10 euros y se obtienen los mismos aciertos que si se apuestan 5. Los premios pueden consultarse en la web de ONCE. Juega al cupón diario de la ONCE, Super ONCE, Triplex y gana miles de premios. El Triplex de la ONCE es un sorteo que forma parte de la línea de apuestas que ofrece la Organización Nacional de Ciegos (ONCE). El Triplex se puede jugar hasta cinco veces al día y por tan solo 50 céntimos, que es lo que cuesta un boleto. Comprueba en la página web de MARCA si has sido uno de los afortunados en el sorteo del Triplex. Puedes hacerte con premios de hasta 150 euros. Primer sorteo: 123 Segundo sorteo: 841 Tercer sorteo: 285 Cuarto sorteo: 253 Quinto sorteo: 511 Jugar al sorteo del Triplex es una tarea sencilla. En este aspecto, se deben seleccionar tres cifras consecutivas, con las que se podrá jugar un sorteo o los cinco que hay diarios. Si se hace una apuesta múltiple, se jugarán los sorteos siguientes a la hora de la apuesta realizada. El premio más grande del Triplex es de 150 euros, si se consigue acertar las tres cifras en el mismo orden de extracción. El siguiente premio es de 10 euros, si se aciertan las cifras en distinto orden. El premio será de dos euros si se aciertan las dos primeras o las dos últimas, y el reintegro será si has acertado un número de la primera fila o de la última. articles.title: Roku's new Labs hub brings experimental apps to the big screen | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Roku’s latest OS update introduces Roku Labs, a new hub for experimental apps, alongside personalized home screens in more markets, streaming subscription bundles, and more.
articles.body:
Roku is turning your TV into its own testing grounds. On Thursday, the connected TV device maker unveiled the latest update to Roku OS, which introduces a new experience called Roku Labs that allows U.S. customers to access experimental apps made by the company.

These still-in-development apps will be accessible through a new tile on Roku’s Home Screen. Initially, users will see apps for tracking the weather, stocks, and a new game called Roku Dash. The latter involves customers flying a UFO across “Roku City,” the company’s default screensaver of a neon purple and pink city skyline, interspersed with references to pop culture and ads.

The additions suggest Roku is increasing its investment in what could turn out to be monetizable first-party apps that put the company at the center of connected households. Today, the streaming device and TV maker competes with often more advanced AI-powered connected TV products from rivals like Google and Amazon, powered by their assistants, Gemini and Alexa+.

Alongside this update, Roku is making its newer, personalized Home Screen available in new markets, including Mexico and Brazil, where it will offer region-specific features like localized content and tailored suggestions. In addition, Roku’s Voice assistant will now be able to answer weather-related questions.

On the streaming side, Roku will begin offering bundled subscriptions in the U.S. and Mexico that let you mix-and-match streaming plans from smaller services like AMC+, Fox ONE, Hallmark+, Howdy, and Starz. These bundles are usually more affordable than purchasing each plan à la carte.

Roku also said it is open-sourcing the software that powers its Roku remote, Roku LT OS, which could invite outside developers and makers to build their own applications and devices.

articles.title: Lokayukta police trap GST official with Rs 8 lakh bribe
articles.summary: Lokayukta police trap Bengaluru Central GST superintendent accepting Rs 8 lakh bribe via agent; both arrested under Prevention of Corruption Act.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Lokayukta police Thursday trapped a Central GST official while accepting a bribe of Rs 8 lakh through a middleman.GST superintendent Mohit Pratap Singh (south division-4, A-range, south commissionerate), had demanded Rs 20 lakh from a businessman dealing with iron materials to close a case registered against him, according to Lokayukta police. Besides Singh, police also arrested his agent Salman Sheik.“The city-based businessman was booked for evading tax. However, the complaint was false and Singh knew it. When the businessman approached Singh seeking a solution, Singh promised to close the case once for all and demanded a Rs 20-lakh bribe. Finally, Singh agreed to take Rs 8 lakh and directed the businessman to hand over the money to his agent Salman Sheik,” Lokayukta police said.“The businessman approached us and registered a case against Singh and Sheik under the Prevention of Corruption Act. We laid the trap and directed the businessman to hand over the cash to Sheik, who was waiting near Singh’s chamber in Kendriya Sadan, Koramangala. The raids were carried out when Singh received the cash from Sheik,” the anti-corruption police said.Singh and Sheik were sent to judicial custody in Bengaluru central prison.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: Hasan Piker insists Middle East would be 'more stable' if Iran had nuclear weapons during Axios interview
articles.summary: In an interview with Axios, progressive Twitch streamer Hasan Piker said the Middle East would be "more stable" if Iran had nuclear weapons.
articles.body: Progressive commentator Hasan Piker is not opposed to Iran having nuclear weapons, according to comments he made in an interview with Axios. "Do you think Iran should be free to build a nuclear weapon?" Axios correspondent Alex Thompson asked in a clip that aired Thursday on CNN. "I think Iran, much like any other sovereign nation, has a right to defend itself, regardless of its domestic policies," Piker responded. RADICAL EL-SAYED ALLY DOUBLES DOWN ON ANTI-AMERICAN RHETORIC WITH STUNNING TERRORISM COMPARISON The popular Twitch streamer went on to cite political scientist John Mearsheimer in the belief that "mutually assured destruction is the only way for countries to have sovereignty," something he said would bring regional stability. "Now having said that, do I want Iran to have nuclear arms? No. But I also don't want America, or Russia, or China to have a nuclear arms either," Piker said. "Do you think the Middle East would be more stable if Iran had a nuclear weapon?" Thompson followed. "I believe yes. I think that the Middle East would be more stable," Piker responded. ABDUL EL-SAYED DISMISSES QUESTIONS ABOUT HASAN PIKER TIES ON 'FACE THE NATION,' PIVOTS TO GROCERIES The far-left personality went on to stress that he's not "advocating" for a nuclear-armed Iran or that it should have weapons-grade enriched uranium, but he insisted that the nuclear conversation is a "distraction." "Time and time again, they have shown, the Iranian government, regardless of whether you want to trust them or not, you can just look at their actions, have proven that they are utilizing the conversation of enriched uranium as a point of leverage to bring America back to the table to get sanctions relief," Piker said. CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS Piker began generating headlines earlier in the day when he claimed the U.S. is responsible for more terrorism than al Qaeda "pound for pound." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Democratic Michigan Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, who campaigned alongside Piker during the primary, has repeatedly been asked about Piker's commentary and has attempted to distance himself from his latest comments. "I do not agree with this statement [on al Qaeda], nor do I give much weight to the statements made by a social media streamer," El-Sayed said. "I am more concerned with the dangerous policies of Donald Trump and Mike Rogers that are raising the prices of gas, groceries and healthcare for Michiganders."

articles.title: Lions vs. Bills live updates, inactives, where to watch: Ed Oliver suffers injury, ruled out ahead of new Highmark Stadium christening on 'Thursday Night Football'
articles.summary: The Bills host the Lions on Thursday Night Football in Week 2.
articles.body: Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season kicks off tonight as the Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions star in what should be a "Thursday Night Football" matchup for the ages.Though both teams entered the year with plenty of hype, they're entering Week 2 with vastly different momentum coming off their respective season openers. Josh Allen and the Bills came up clutch in a Sunday afternoon thriller against the Texans, walking away with a 36-31 win thanks to a 96-yard drive to take the lead on an Allen-to-Joshua-Palmer touchdown with 1:36 remaining in the fourth. Buffalo's defense closed it out, forcing C.J. Stroud's second lost fumble of the day — an all-around effort.The Lions appeared to be on track for dominance in Week 1, entering the game as 7-point favorites over the New Orleans Saints before getting off to an early 21-0 lead. Things fell apart quickly for the Lions' defense in the second half, however, allowing the Tyler Shough-led Saints to tie it up to force overtime. The Lions scored a touchdown to open OT, and the Saints responded with a score of their own. But the Saints' failed 2-point conversion after the touchdown gave Detroit the surprisingly hard-fought win, giving the Lions plenty to consider when shaping their game plan against Allen & Co.Where to watch Lions vs. Bills tonightLions-Bills start time: 8:15 p.m. ETLocation: Highmark Stadium | Orchard Park, N.Y.TV channel/live stream: Amazon PrimeFollow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Bills host the Lions on Thursday Night Football in Week 2.

articles.title: El-Sayed tries to put the Hasan Piker debate behind him as midterms approach
articles.summary: Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed repeatedly deflected calls to disavow Twitch streamer Hasan Piker's controversial rhetoric.
articles.body: Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed has faced backlash for months over his relationship with Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, who is known for his controversial rhetoric. The candidate has yet to disavow Piker and now seems to be tiring of the questions, looking to shift focus to the issues that he says are really at the heart of the race. El-Sayed's relationship with Piker was scrutinized before the two of them appeared at a campaign event in April 2026. On March 30, El-Sayed posted a video with the caption "Let's talk about Hasan." In the video, the Michigan Democrat explained that he was looking for a way to access people who "feel locked out of our politics," saying that they are the same people who Piker speaks to through his daily streams. He went on to clarify where he agrees with Piker, which included the streamer's stances on the war in Iran, AIPAC's involvement in U.S. politics and healthcare. "Now, he streams for eight hours a day, every day. A lot of the things that he said, I might not agree with, but that doesn't mean I'm not going to have a conversation with him, and that doesn't mean that the people who listen to him don't deserve to listen to their politicians and to have a pathway into politics to vote for the things that they need and deserve," El-Sayed said. ABDUL EL-SAYED SAYS RALLYING WITH HASAN PIKER DOESN'T MEAN HE ENDORSES 'AMERICA DESERVED 9/11' REMARK The Michigan Democrat joined "FOX & Friends" ahead of his event with Piker, where he said that appearing with someone did not mean that he agreed with them. While he did not disavow Piker specifically, he referred to the streamer's past remarks, saying, "Of course, I oppose rape. Of course, I don't think 9/11 was justified." Amid the scrutiny of his decision to campaign with Piker, El-Sayed repeatedly blamed the criticism on "cancel culture" and insisted that Democrats needed to be willing to speak with people at their level. The event with Piker went on as planned, but El-Sayed still faced questions. He was asked while standing next to Piker to disavow the streamer's past rhetoric, which he refused to do. "I'm not here to disavow people's views. I'm here to have a conversation about how to get money out of politics, put money back in pockets, and pass Medicare for all. That's the conversation that folks are here to listen to," El-Sayed said in response. EL-SAYED PALS AROUND WITH FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER THE DAY BEFORE CRUCIAL MICHIGAN SENATE ELECTION The controversy surrounding the April campus appearance would set off a months-long line of questioning, with El-Sayed repeatedly walking the line between condemning some of Piker's rhetoric without going into specifics or alienating the streamer's audience. This became more common after El-Sayed defeated Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., in the Democratic primary in August. Following El-Sayed's victory, Piker called for those who opposed the Michigan Democrat to be "punished" by the party. "You can't be out here saying like, 'Oh, I'm a centrist Democrat. And I think Abdul is a bridge too far.' That must be punished," Piker said. After his primary victory, El-Sayed was asked in multiple interviews to comment on Piker's past rhetoric. When CNN's Kaitlan Collins asked El-Sayed whether he would renounce Piker in August, something that Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., had urged him to do, the Michigan Democrat said he was "less focused on folks who are campaigning with me, more focused on the folks I'm campaigning to." A few days later, El-Sayed was asked about Piker again, this time during an appearance on NBC's "Meet the Press." In response to host Kristen Welker's question, El-Sayed repeated what he said on CNN about focusing more on voters than those who appear with him on the campaign trail. Shortly after El-Sayed's appearance on "Meet the Press," Piker drew the ire of several lawmakers on both sides of the aisle after making a comment that some interpreted as blaming antisemitic attacks on American Jews' support of Israel. "People don't f--- with Israel any longer. And if Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they're singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone will come around and take action not against Israel, mind you, but against American Jews," Piker said during his Aug. 20 stream. HASAN PIKER CALLS FOR DEMOCRATS WHO OPPOSE ABDUL EL-SAYED TO BE 'PUNISHED' The comment set off a wave of condemnations from lawmakers, including Sens. Cory Booker, D-N.J.; Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich.; and Jacky Rosen, D-Nev.; House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y.; and Reps. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J.; Ritchie Torres, D-N.Y.; Jared Moskowitz, D-Fla.; Brad Schneider, D-Ill.; Greg Stanton, D-Ariz.; and Hillary Scholten, D-Mich. El-Sayed issued a statement in which he seemed to distance himself from Piker amid the backlash. "I believe all Americans deserve the right to advocate for what they believe without fear of violence. This is particularly true for communities that have been intimidated for their beliefs in the past," El-Sayed wrote on X. "My commitment to Jewish safety is the same as my commitment to the safety of my own daughters," he added. "Antisemitism is a scourge, and we need to address it in all its forms. And I stand against any rhetoric that puts the community at risk." Shortly after the controversy over Piker's remarks, El-Sayed told Semafor that he had "no plans" to campaign with the streamer. However, this did not stop the press from asking the Michigan Democrat about Piker. During an appearance on "The Breakfast Club" in late August, El-Sayed framed criticism of his ties to Piker as a form of "cancel culture," saying that there was a "massive effort to cancel Hasan." "I think we've got to stop with the cancel culture. It's not about, like, 'Where are you on this one individual?' It's more, 'Do you agree or disagree with the thing that the person said?' And, the thing about it is, that, like, when we play as if the whole person can be reduced to a single soundbite that you took out of context, you're not, you're not dealing with real life," El-Sayed said. ABDUL EL-SAYED DISMISSES QUESTIONS ABOUT HASAN PIKER TIES ON 'FACE THE NATION,' PIVOTS TO GROCERIES El-Sayed's exasperation with the media's questions about Piker became apparent during a Sept. 13 appearance on "Face the Nation." When CBS News' Weijia Jiang asked El-Sayed about Jewish Michiganders' concerns regarding his ties to Piker, the Michigan Democrat appeared to be fed up. "Weijia, with all due respect, this is the third time you’ve asked about a Twitch streamer in California. I’ve done four events in Michigan this week. You know what didn’t come up? Twitch streamers in California," El-Sayed responded. The candidate said that voters would rather discuss grocery prices, healthcare and the environment, among other things. "I’m not interested in having a conversation about streamers in California because they are not raising the prices of gas and groceries," El-Sayed added. articles.title: Dave Rubin breaks down Hasan Piker's transition from Twitch streamer to political player
articles.summary: Dave Rubin recalls how Hasan Piker rose from Cenk Uygur's The Young Turks to becoming a leading voice among Democratic Socialists on Twitch.
articles.body: Hasan Piker may be a major name in online political media now, but when he got his start at The Young Turks, a network co-founded by his uncle, Cenk Uygur, he was a young, loud guy looking to make a splash in the online political discourse. Dave Rubin, who formerly worked on The Young Turks, recalls Piker as "a big dude" who was "really loud." "[Cenk] just put Hasan on air, even though virtually everyone there wanted to be on air," Rubin recalled in a conversation with Fox News Digital. Rubin said that most of the staff at The Young Turks wanted to be on camera, but "once [Hasan] just showed up, he just got on camera. Cenk just gave him the keys to the kingdom and I guess he became some sort of personality since then." While Piker has continued to profess anti-capitalist and progressive views while building an audience of loyal followers, Rubin later had a political epiphany and realigned himself with the right. In a 2017 PragerU video, Rubin explained that the left had gone from being "progressive to regressive," pointing to cancel culture and calls for censorship, among other things. HASAN PIKER IS BECOMING THE 'FACE OF THE PROGRESSIVE MOVEMENT,' FORMER DEMOCRATIC OPERATIVE WARNS Rubin said he was not surprised that Piker had gone from Twitch streamer to what he called the "brain trust" of Democratic Socialists. "The Rubin Report" host explained that he saw Piker as filling a void for the left as the right saw a rise in online personalities. Rubin also pointed to the ways in which Piker differed from the typical left-leaning personalities, which he said have made the Twitch streamer resonate with young people. "There weren't that many entertaining new people on the left online. As I said, the right had this rich group of people that was growing and growing and going, whether it was Ben Shapiro or Jordan Peterson or me or Steven Crowder or whoever it might be. There was this long list of people. The left had a couple people…. They were all sort of dorky, effeminate, weird, kind of limp-wristed, low testosterone," Rubin said. "And he came on, and again, he's big, he kind of jacked, you know, he wears his fancy clothes, he is aggressive, it's not really what progressives are," he said. Beyond Piker’s physical presence and media rise, Rubin argued that the streamer's ideology is anchored in an aggressive critique of Israel, something that he said has become more common among left-wing personalities. He argued that progressives "have an endless obsession and hatred of Israel," which he said "is just an extension of hatred of the Jews." FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER EQUATES ISRAEL'S 'RIGHT TO EXIST' TO NAZI GERMANY "You don't have to agree with everything any government does or anything else, but when you have no standards for any other country, and then you hold only one country to any standard whatsoever, and that country happens to be the place where the Jews live, maybe it has a little something to do with Jews," Rubin said. Piker has faced accusations of antisemitism and sparked backlash with a recent comment about Jewish Americans' support for Israel. During his Aug. 20 stream, Piker said, "People don't f--- with Israel any longer. And if Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they're singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone will come around and take action not against Israel, mind you, but against American Jews." Several lawmakers condemned the remarks, including House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y. Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, who campaigned with Piker, responded to the streamer's remarks, saying "I believe all Americans deserve the right to advocate for what they believe without fear of violence." EL-SAYED DISTANCES HIMSELF FROM HASAN PIKER AFTER DISTURBING REMARKS ABOUT JEWISH AMERICANS Rubin believes that one of the reasons behind the focus on Israel is that "Jews don't fit into the intersectional calculator." He said that, while Jews had been historically persecuted, their success in America has made it so they don't fit the mold of an "oppressed minority" the way other groups do. "If you're an oppressed group that's not oppressed, it debunks their whole ideology," Rubin said. According to Rubin, the central hypocrisy comes down to Piker's lifestyle versus the beliefs the streamer professes to hold. This dynamic, Rubin warns, could leave Piker's audience bearing the consequences of his ideas. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE "I have no doubt he lives like a capitalist while promoting socialism, and he won't be eaten by the revolution the way some average kid who gets confused by his ideas and then probably gets out there and does something stupid will," Rubin said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital reached out to Piker and The Young Turks for comment.

After suffering a hamstring injury during Wednesday's practice, he was not on the field Friday as the team continued preparing for the Cincinnati Bengals.According to KPRC2's Aaron Wilson, Collins is dealing with a Grade 1 hamstring strain and is not expected to play on Sunday.Collins isn't the only wide receiver at risk of missing Week 2. Both Lamar Jackson and Justin Herbert each could be without key weapons on Sunday.In Baltimore, Ravens wideout Zay Flowers left a Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts with a hamstring injury. That issue had kept him out of practice all week after head coach Jesse Minter had labeled him day-to-day, but he was back on the field on Friday. Jackson will already not have Ja'Kobi Lane as a target after the rookie was placed on injured reserve following wrist surgery.Ladd McConkey was at Los Angeles Chargers' practice on Thursday, but working off to the side. The wide receiver suffered a rib injury during their Week 1 loss to the Arizona Cardinals and was also said to be day-to-day.Other receivers at risk of missing Week 2 include Chris Olave (hamstring) of the New Orleans Saints and Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) of the Jacksonville Jaguars.Cooper Rush will start again for the Atlanta Falcons with Jack Strand backing him up. Tua Tagovailoa is not fully recovered from the oblique injury that kept him from playing in Week 1 and Michael Penix Jr. (ACL) is "close" to returning, but has been ruled out.Other Week 2 injuries to monitor: Kyler Murray (concussion) was limited during Thursday's practice after suffering a concussion in Week 1 against the Green Bay Packers. If the Minnesota Vikings quarterback is not cleared in time, Carson Wentz will get the start against the Chicago Bears.New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) will play Week 2 against the Steelers, he told reporters on Thursday. The veteran sat out Week 1 with a knee sprain, but also declared himself fit to play against the Ravens this week. "I'm going," Kamara said. "If it wasn't right, I wouldn't be in. articles.title: WWE SmackDown live now (Sept. 18): Results, grades as Sami Zayn's title reign begins tonight
articles.summary: "WWE SmackDown" is back in the U.S. after last week's stunning CM Punk vs. Sami Zayn world title change. Follow live results and play-by-play of the action here.
articles.body: "WWE SmackDown" is in Corpus Christi, Texas on this Friday, Sept. 18, following last week's stunning CM Punk vs. Sami Zayn world title change in Mexico. After Zayn's return to world champion status, expect plenty of chaotic fallout. Follow tonight's "WWE SmackDown" live results and play-by-play to catch all the action here.It took a boatload of shenanigans in their main-event rematch last Friday, but Zayn ultimately got the job done after interference from Kevin Owens, Johnny Gargano and Candice LeRae. The win cuts short Punk's latest title reign, which began in July at the expense of Zayn over on "Raw." Last week, Zayn promised Gargano a shot at the gold if he regained it. We'll see where things go with Money In the Bank around the corner.Regarding Money In the Bank, wrestlers are still qualifying for the upcoming ladder matches. Tonight, Alexa Bliss gets back in action after suffering her kayfabe arm injury at the hands of Jade Cargill. Standing in her way are former world champion Cargill and current Women's U.S. Champion Jacy Jayne.Cody Rhodes was absent from last week's "SmackDown" following his Sunday Night's Main Event loss to Randy Orton, who firmly set his sights on the world title prior to the Zayn-Punk rematch. Tonight, Rhodes is expected to speak in a sit-down interview, while Orton takes part in a men's Money In the Bank qualifier against Trick Williams and Rey Fenix.Check out Friday night's full "WWE SmackDown" lineup below, which starts at 8 p.m. ET on USA Network:Undisputed WWE Championship: Sami Zayn (c.) vs. Kevin OwensWomen's Money in the Bank qualifying match: Alexa Bliss vs. Jade Cargill vs. Jacy JayneMen's Money in the Bank qualifying match: Randy Orton vs. Trick Williams vs. Rey FenixFor complete coverage of tonight's "WWE SmackDown" on USA Network, follow along with Uncrowned's live blog below:

articles.summary: Follow Isaac "Pitbull" Cruz vs. Nestor Bravo live results and round-by-round updates for the Cruz vs. Bravo fight card on Saturday night in San Diego.
articles.body: Uncrowned has Isaac "Pitbull" Cruz vs. Nestor Bravo live results, round-by-round updates, highlights, ring walks and start time for the Cruz vs. Bravo fight card on Saturday night at Pechanga Arena in San Diego, California. Isaac “Pitbull” Cruz defends his WBC interim super lightweight title against Nestor Bravo in the night's main event.Cruz (28-3-2, 18 KOs) became WBC interim super lightweight champion with a unanimous decision victory over Omar Salcido in July 2025. The former WBA champion then retained his interim title with a majority draw against Lamont Roach Jr. in December, and now makes his second defense of the WBC’s interim belt.Bravo (24-1, 17 KOs) gets his first opportunity at the world level after returning to his winning ways with a Knockout of the Year contender over Pedro Campa. Jesus Ramos Jr. (24-1, 19 KOs) was expected to put his WBC interim middleweight title on the line against Meiirim Nursultanov (20-0, 11 KOs) in the night's co-feature, however that fight was ultimately scrapped Friday after Ramos was hospitalized, having fallen ill.The Cruz vs. Bravo fight card starts at 8 p.m. ET on DAZN, with main event ring walks expected around 11 p.m. ET.Follow all of the action with Uncrowned's live results and play-by-play of the main card below.Main card (8 p.m. ET, DAZN)WBC interim super lightweight title: Isaac Cruz vs. Nestor BravoSuper middleweight: Daniel Blancas vs. Sergio JimenezMiddleweight: Marco Verde vs. Guillermo HernandezMiddleweight: Eumir Marcial vs. Omar Ulises Huerta
